description:
Alcohol in ice cream!....Indulge in the ultimate creamy Peanut Butter Baileys Gelato—a rich, decadent treat with no added sugar! This science-based recipe breaks down the secrets of gelato texture, balancing fats, and sugar to create a smooth and scoopable dessert. 🍨✨

Learn how to achieve perfect gelato structure while keeping it super low in sugar without compromising flavor or texture. We’ll touch on the subject of types of alcohol, what it does, the issues with alcohol in ice cream and more. 

Plus...this is Episode 1 of the new "Alcoholic Ice Cream" series so buckle up, let's get drunk! 🥴 😂

📌 What You’ll Learn in This Video:
✅ The role of fats and solids in Gelato
✅ How to keep gelato soft and scoopable without added sugar
✅ The impact of alcohol (Baileys!) on freezing point depression
✅ Step-by-step recipe with pro tips for home gelato makers

🔬 This is a science-based food video, so whether you’re a gelato enthusiast, food science nerd, or just love a good boozy dessert, you’re in the right place!

🔔 Don’t forget to LIKE, SUBSCRIBE, and hit the BELL for more food science and ice cream-making videos!

#PeanutButterGelato #NoSugarAdded #BaileysGelato #FoodScience #GelatoMaking #HomemadeGelato #IceCreamScience #HealthyDessert #LowSugarIceCream #CookingWithAlcohol #FoodTech #KitchenChemistry

comments.text: Thanks Nick. I really enjoy the episodes that have a little bit of chemistry thrown in along with the explanations. I use small amounts of alcohol occasionally for freeze depression (at your suggestion) and it works very well. These are small amounts of Vodka in the range of 5ml or 10ml. Perhaps in the future there could be some discussion on the use of artificial flavours and colouring agents (gels) and how they may affect ice cream batching. Three days ago, I batched some black ice cream with Anise flavour. Really outstanding. I have noticed yesterday there is some softening of the ice cream after a rather good initial freezing. My freezer is at -22.4C. Research seems to indicate that some of the ingredients in the black gel colouring can affect freeze point, texture etc. The manufacturer was kind enough to give me the percentages of the ingredients and now I am trying get my head wrapped around all of this. I have not yet received the technical information yet on the Anise flavour. More fun in the kitchen!
